#### Define theme and load libraries
```{r}

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

my_ggplot_theme <- theme_classic() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(size = 0.8),
    legend.position = c(0.66, 0.12),  # Position the legend inside the plot, above X-axis
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
  )
```

### Raincloud plot panel A
```{r}

# Read the data from a CSV file
data <- read_csv("../input/af3/af3_fullcomplex.csv")

# Convert Known_outcome to a factor and define group
# Ensure the x-axis is ordered as Non-Perceived then Perceived within each group
data <- data %>%
  mutate(Known_outcome = factor(Known_outcome, levels = c("No perception", "Perception")),
         Group = factor(ifelse(receptor == "AtFLS2", "AtFLS2", "Non-AtFLS2"), levels = c("AtFLS2", "Non-AtFLS2")))

# Assess normality using Shapiro-Wilk test for each receptor group separately
shapiro_results <- data %>%
  group_by(Group, Known_outcome) %>%
  summarise(shapiro_p_value = shapiro.test(`ipTM flg22_FLS2`)$p.value)

print("Shapiro-Wilk Test for Normality:")
print(shapiro_results)

# Perform statistical tests separately for each receptor group
test_results <- data %>%
  group_by(Group) %>%
  summarise(
    test_name = ifelse(any(shapiro.test(`ipTM flg22_FLS2`)$p.value < 0.05), "Wilcoxon rank-sum test", "t-test"),
    p_value = ifelse(any(shapiro.test(`ipTM flg22_FLS2`)$p.value < 0.05),
                      wilcox.test(`ipTM flg22_FLS2` ~ Known_outcome, data = .)$p.value,
                      t.test(`ipTM flg22_FLS2` ~ Known_outcome, data = .)$p.value)
  )

print("Statistical Test Results:")
print(test_results)

# Creating the combined raincloud plot
p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = interaction(Group, Known_outcome, lex.order = TRUE), 
                      y = `ipTM flg22_FLS2`, fill = Known_outcome)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.5, color = NA, show.legend = FALSE, scale = "width", width = 0.4) +  # Density plot
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.09, outlier.shape = NA, show.legend = FALSE, color = "black", alpha = 0.8) +  # Slightly wider boxplot
  geom_jitter(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.6, color = "black", width = 0.1, show.legend = FALSE) +  # Less prominent points
  labs(title = "Raincloud Plot of ipTM flg22_FLS2 by Experimental Result and Receptor Type",
       x = "Experimental Result (Grouped by Receptor Type)",
       y = "ipTM flg22_FLS2") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#fd5901", "#4477aa")) +
  my_ggplot_theme  # Apply custom ggplot theme


p
# Save the plot
ggsave("../output/af3/raincloud_combined.pdf", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)

```


###ROC curves using different metrics
```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(pROC)
library(readr)  # Use read_csv from readr

# Read the data from the CSV file
data <- read_csv("../input/af3/af3_fullcomplex.csv")

# Ensure the experimental results are properly formatted
data$Known_outcome <- as.factor(data$Known_outcome)

# Transform PAE data by adding a negative sign before analysis
data$`Pae min flg22_FLS2` <- -data$`Pae min flg22_FLS2`
data$`Pae min flg22_coreceptor` <- -data$`Pae min flg22_coreceptor`

# Define predictive metrics for analysis
predictive_metrics <- c("ipTM flg22_FLS2", "ipTM_flg22_coreceptor", 
                        "Pae min flg22_FLS2", "Pae min flg22_coreceptor")

# Initialize a list to store ROC results
roc_results <- list()

# Calculate ROC curves and AUC for each predictive metric
for (metric in predictive_metrics) {
  roc_results[[metric]] <- roc(response = data$Known_outcome, predictor = data[[metric]])
}

# Extract AUC values for each metric
auc_values <- sapply(roc_results, auc)

# Assign specific colors for each metric
color_matrix <- c(
  "ipTM flg22_FLS2" = "#845ec2",
  "ipTM_flg22_coreceptor" = "#5dc4c9",
  "Pae min flg22_FLS2" = "#117733",
  "Pae min flg22_coreceptor" = "#ddcc77"
)

# Order metrics by AUC values
ordered_metrics <- names(sort(auc_values, decreasing = TRUE))

# Prepare data for plotting
roc_coords <- lapply(roc_results, function(roc_obj) {
  coords(roc_obj, "all", ret = c("specificity", "sensitivity"))
})

roc_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(roc_coords), function(metric_name) {
  data.frame(
    Metric = metric_name,
    Specificity = 1 - roc_coords[[metric_name]]$specificity,
    Sensitivity = roc_coords[[metric_name]]$sensitivity
  )
}))
# Convert "Metric" to factor with the same level order as ordered_metrics
roc_data$Metric <- factor(roc_data$Metric, levels = ordered_metrics)

# Plot the ROC curves using ggplot2 (minimal changes below)
roc_plot <- ggplot(roc_data, aes(x = Specificity, y = Sensitivity, color = Metric)) +
  geom_line(size = 1, show.legend = TRUE) +
  geom_line(
    data = data.frame(x = c(0, 1), y = c(0, 1)), 
    aes(x, y), 
    linetype = "dashed", 
    color = "darkgrey"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = color_matrix,
    breaks = ordered_metrics,   # Ensure order and matching with factor levels
    labels = paste(
      ordered_metrics,
      "(AUC:", round(auc_values[ordered_metrics], 3), ")"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "ROC Curves for Predictive Metrics", 
    x = "False Positive Rate", 
    y = "True Positive Rate"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = c(0, 0), 
    limits = c(0, 1), 
    breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), 
    labels = c("0", "0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "1")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = c(0, 0), 
    limits = c(0, 1), 
    breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), 
    labels = c("0", "0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "1")
  ) +
  my_ggplot_theme

# Print and save the plot
print(roc_plot)
ggsave("../output/af3/ROC_multiple_metrics.pdf", 
       plot = roc_plot, width = 6.5, height = 6, dpi = 300)

```

### ROC curves on different receptor subset
```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(pROC)
library(readr)  # Use read_csv from readr

# Read the data from the CSV file
data <- read_csv("../input/af3/af3_fullcomplex.csv")  

# Ensure the experimental results are properly formatted
data$Known_outcome <- as.factor(data$Known_outcome)

# Subset data for the three groups
data_all <- data
data_AtFLS2 <- data[data$receptor == "AtFLS2", ]
data_no_AtFLS2 <- data[data$receptor != "AtFLS2", ]

# Calculate ROC curves for each subset
roc_all <- roc(response = data_all$Known_outcome, predictor = data_all$"ipTM flg22_FLS2")
roc_AtFLS2 <- roc(response = data_AtFLS2$Known_outcome, predictor = data_AtFLS2$"ipTM flg22_FLS2")
roc_no_AtFLS2 <- roc(response = data_no_AtFLS2$Known_outcome, predictor = data_no_AtFLS2$"ipTM flg22_FLS2")

# Extract AUC values
auc_all <- auc(roc_all)
auc_AtFLS2 <- auc(roc_AtFLS2)
auc_no_AtFLS2 <- auc(roc_no_AtFLS2)

# Extract coordinates for the ROC curves
coords_all <- coords(roc_all, "all", ret = c("threshold", "sensitivity", "specificity", "accuracy"))
coords_AtFLS2 <- coords(roc_AtFLS2, "all", ret = c("threshold", "sensitivity", "specificity", "accuracy"))
coords_no_AtFLS2 <- coords(roc_no_AtFLS2, "all", ret = c("threshold", "sensitivity", "specificity", "accuracy"))

# Convert to data frames for ggplot
coords_all_df <- as.data.frame(coords_all)
coords_AtFLS2_df <- as.data.frame(coords_AtFLS2)
coords_no_AtFLS2_df <- as.data.frame(coords_no_AtFLS2)

my_ggplot_theme <- theme_classic() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(size = 0.8),
    legend.position = c(0.66, 0.12),  # Position the legend inside the plot, above X-axis
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
  )

# Plot the ROC curves using ggplot2
roc_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = coords_all_df, aes(x = 1 - specificity, y = sensitivity, color = "All data"), size = 1.2) +
  geom_line(data = coords_AtFLS2_df, aes(x = 1 - specificity, y = sensitivity, color = "AtFLS2"), size = 1.2) +
  geom_line(data = coords_no_AtFLS2_df, aes(x = 1 - specificity, y = sensitivity, color = "Non-AtFLS2"), size = 1.2) +
  geom_line(data = data.frame(x = c(0, 1), y = c(0, 1)), aes(x, y), linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgrey") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "All data" = "#4477aa",
    "AtFLS2" = "#5dc4c9",
    "Non-AtFLS2" = "#117733"
  ), labels = c(
    paste("All data (AUC:", round(auc_all, 3), ")"),
    paste("AtFLS2 (AUC:", round(auc_AtFLS2, 3), ")"),
    paste("Non-AtFLS2 (AUC:", round(auc_no_AtFLS2, 3), ")")
  )) +
  labs(title = "ROC Curves for Different Receptor Subsets", 
       x = "False Positive Rate", y = "True Positive Rate", color = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), labels = c("0", "0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "1")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), labels = c("0", "0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "1")) +
  my_ggplot_theme

# Print the plot
print(roc_plot)

# Save the plot
ggsave("../output/af3/ROC_receptor_subset.pdf", plot = roc_plot, width = 6.5, height = 6, dpi = 300)



```


### Accuracy curves on receptor
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

#setwd("~/FLS2_engineering/R_ploting/script/")

# Define customized ggplot theme
my_ggplot_theme <- theme_classic() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
        axis.ticks = element_line(size = 0.8),
        legend.position = c(0.85, 0.2), # Adjust position to bottom right above x-axis
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black"),
        legend.title = element_blank(), # Remove the legend title for a cleaner look
        legend.text = element_text(size = 14))

# Read and prepare the data
data <- read.csv("../input/af3/af3_fullcomplex.csv")

# Define the range of cutoffs
cutoffs <- seq(0.7, 0.9, by = 0.01)

# Function to calculate accuracy for a given subset of data
calculate_accuracy <- function(data_subset) {
  expanded_data <- data_subset %>% 
    crossing(Cutoff = cutoffs) %>% 
    mutate(
      Cutoff = as.numeric(Cutoff),
      Accurate = ifelse(ipTM.flg22_FLS2 >= Cutoff & Known_outcome == "Perception" |
                        ipTM.flg22_FLS2 < Cutoff & Known_outcome == "No perception", 1, 0)
    ) %>% 
    group_by(Cutoff) %>% 
    summarise(
      Accuracy = mean(Accurate),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )
  return(expanded_data)
}

# Calculate accuracy for all data, only AtFLS2, and non-AtFLS2
accuracy_all <- calculate_accuracy(data)
accuracy_AtFLS2 <- calculate_accuracy(data[data$receptor == "AtFLS2", ])
accuracy_non_AtFLS2 <- calculate_accuracy(data[data$receptor != "AtFLS2", ])

# Find the optimal cutoff where accuracy is maximum for each group
optimal_cutoff_all <- accuracy_all$Cutoff[which.max(accuracy_all$Accuracy)]
max_accuracy_all <- max(accuracy_all$Accuracy)

optimal_cutoff_AtFLS2 <- accuracy_AtFLS2$Cutoff[which.max(accuracy_AtFLS2$Accuracy)]
max_accuracy_AtFLS2 <- max(accuracy_AtFLS2$Accuracy)

optimal_cutoff_non_AtFLS2 <- accuracy_non_AtFLS2$Cutoff[which.max(accuracy_non_AtFLS2$Accuracy)]
max_accuracy_non_AtFLS2 <- max(accuracy_non_AtFLS2$Accuracy)

# Output results
cat("All Data - Optimal ipTM Cutoff:", optimal_cutoff_all, "\n")
cat("All Data - Highest Accuracy:", max_accuracy_all * 100, "%\n")
cat("AtFLS2 - Optimal ipTM Cutoff:", optimal_cutoff_AtFLS2, "\n")
cat("AtFLS2 - Highest Accuracy:", max_accuracy_AtFLS2 * 100, "%\n")
cat("Non-AtFLS2 - Optimal ipTM Cutoff:", optimal_cutoff_non_AtFLS2, "\n")
cat("Non-AtFLS2 - Highest Accuracy:", max_accuracy_non_AtFLS2 * 100, "%\n")

# Plotting
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = accuracy_all, aes(x = Cutoff, y = Accuracy, color = "All Data"), size = 1) +
  geom_line(data = accuracy_AtFLS2, aes(x = Cutoff, y = Accuracy, color = "AtFLS2"), size = 1) +
  geom_line(data = accuracy_non_AtFLS2, aes(x = Cutoff, y = Accuracy, color = "Non-AtFLS2"), size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = optimal_cutoff_all, linetype = "dashed", color = "#4477aa", size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = optimal_cutoff_AtFLS2, linetype = "dashed", color = "#5dc4c9", size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = optimal_cutoff_non_AtFLS2, linetype = "dashed", color = "#117733", size = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("All Data" = "#4477aa",
                                "AtFLS2" = "#5dc4c9",
                                "Non-AtFLS2" = "#117733")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.4, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)) +
  labs(x = "Average ipTM Threshold", y = "Accuracy", title = "AF3 Accuracy Curves by Receptor Subset") +
  my_ggplot_theme

# Save the plot
ggsave("../output/af3/AF3_accuracy_by_receptor.pdf", dpi = 300, width = 6.6, height = 6)


```

### Accuracy on experimental data
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Load the data
data <- read.csv("../input/af3/af3_fullcomplex.csv")

my_ggplot_theme <- theme_classic() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
        axis.ticks = element_line(size = 0.8))

# Define the cutoff
cutoff <- 0.82

# Calculate accuracy based on the cutoff
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    Accurate = ifelse((ipTM.flg22_FLS2 >= cutoff & Known_outcome == "Perception") | 
                      (ipTM.flg22_FLS2 < cutoff & Known_outcome == "No perception"), 1, 0)
  )

# Group by Known_outcome and calculate accuracy percentage
accuracy_data <- data %>%
  group_by(Known_outcome) %>%
  summarise(
    Accuracy_Percentage = mean(Accurate) * 100,
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Plotting the bar graph
plot <- ggplot(accuracy_data, aes(x = Known_outcome, y = Accuracy_Percentage, fill = Known_outcome)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "",
       x = "Experimental Result",
       y = "% Accuracy (ipTM threshold = 0.82)") +
  my_ggplot_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "none")+
  ylim(0, 100)+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#fd5901", "#4477aa"))  # Color aesthetic based on the experimental result

ggsave("../output/af3/accuracy_on_experimental_data.pdf", plot, width = 4, height = 6)
```


### Accuracy on flg22 variants, using full complex models
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Load and prepare the data
data <- read.csv("../input/af3/af3_fullcomplex.csv") 

# Define filters
receptor_filter <- c("NbFLS2-1", "FLS2XL", "QvFLS2", "TjFLS2", "HlFLS2", 
                     "MdFLS2", "VrFLS2", "FcFLS2", "SlFLS2", "AtFLS2")
ligand_filter <- c("Paeflg22", "Atuflg22", "Rrhflg22", "Rso_1flg22", 
                   "Rso_2flg22", "Ddiflg22", "Eamflg22", "Pviflg22", 
                   "Xfrflg22", "Xorflg22")

# Apply the filter
filtered_data <- data %>%
  filter(receptor %in% receptor_filter, ligand_name %in% ligand_filter)

# Process the filtered data
data_processed <- filtered_data %>%
  mutate(
    Accuracy = ifelse((`ipTM.flg22_FLS2` >= 0.82 & Known_outcome == "Perception") | 
                      (`ipTM.flg22_FLS2` < 0.82 & Known_outcome == "No perception"), 1, 0),
    Type_1_Error = ifelse(`ipTM.flg22_FLS2` >= 0.82 & Known_outcome == "No perception", 1, 0),
    Type_2_Error = ifelse(`ipTM.flg22_FLS2` < 0.82 & Known_outcome == "Perception", 1, 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(ligand_name) %>%
  summarise(
    Accuracy_Percentage = mean(Accuracy) * 100,
    Type_1_Error_Percentage = mean(Type_1_Error) * 100,
    Type_2_Error_Percentage = mean(Type_2_Error) * 100,
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Correctly pivot the data
data_long <- data_processed %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c("Accuracy_Percentage", "Type_1_Error_Percentage", "Type_2_Error_Percentage"),
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Percentage"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Metric = gsub("_Percentage$", "", Metric))

# Set the order of flg22 variants as in the similarity matrix
variant_order <- c("Paeflg22", "Atuflg22", "Rrhflg22", "Rso_1flg22", 
                   "Rso_2flg22", "Ddiflg22", "Eamflg22", "Pviflg22", 
                   "Xfrflg22", "Xorflg22")
data_long$ligand_name <- factor(data_long$ligand_name, levels = rev(variant_order))
data_long$Metric <- factor(data_long$Metric, levels = c("Type_1_Error", "Type_2_Error", "Accuracy"))

# Prepare similarity data
similarity_data <- data.frame(
  ligand_name = variant_order,
  sim = c(100, 50, 36.4, 59.1, 68.2, 63.6, 63.6, 31.8, 59.1, 59.1)
)
similarity_data$ligand_name <- factor(similarity_data$ligand_name, levels = variant_order)

my_ggplot_theme <- theme_classic() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
        axis.ticks = element_line(size = 0.8))

# Plot
stacked_plot <- ggplot(data_long, aes(x = ligand_name, y = Percentage, fill = Metric)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  #coord_flip() +  # This flips the plot to vertical orientation
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Accuracy" = "#4477aa", "Type_1_Error" = "#ee6677", "Type_2_Error" = "#ccbb44")) +
  labs(title = "Metric at ipTM Cutoff 0.82",
       x = "flg22 Variants", y = "Percentage") +
  my_ggplot_theme +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 105)) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0), limits = rev) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom",  # Moves legend to the bottom
        legend.title = element_blank(),  # Optionally remove the legend title
        legend.box = "horizontal",  # Horizontal layout for the legend items
        legend.box.background = element_rect(color="black", size=0.5),  # Adds a box around the legend with a border
        legend.text = element_text(size = 8),  # Adjust text size for better fit
        legend.key.size = unit(0.3, "cm"))  # Adjusts the size of the legend keys

# Add similarity data as a line plot over the bars
final_plot <- stacked_plot +
  geom_line(data = similarity_data, aes(x = ligand_name, y = sim, group = 1), 
            color = "black", size = 1.2, inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = similarity_data, aes(x = ligand_name, y = sim), 
             color = "black", size = 4, inherit.aes = FALSE, 
             shape = 21, fill = "grey", stroke = 1)  # Increased size and added border

# Display the combined plot
print(final_plot)

# Optionally, save the plot
ggsave("../output/af3/combined_accuracy_flg22_similarity_plot.pdf", final_plot, width = 7, height = 5.5)

```


### compare modeling full complex vs FLS2/flg22

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(pROC)
library(readr)

# Read the data from the CSV files
data_fullcomplex <- read_csv("../input/af3/af3_fullcomplex.csv")
data_fls2_flg22 <- read_csv("../input/af3/af3_FLS2_flg22.csv")

# Ensure the experimental results are properly formatted
data_fullcomplex$Known_outcome <- as.factor(data_fullcomplex$Known_outcome)
data_fls2_flg22$Known_outcome <- as.factor(data_fls2_flg22$Known_outcome)

# Transform the predictive metric from "full complex" data
data_fullcomplex$`ipTM flg22_FLS2` <- -data_fullcomplex$`ipTM flg22_FLS2`

# Transform the predictive metric from "Binary FLS2/flg22 modeling" data
data_fls2_flg22$Average_ipTM <- -data_fls2_flg22$Average_ipTM

# Define predictive metrics and labels
metrics <- list(
  "Full Complex Modeling" = list(data = data_fullcomplex, predictor = "ipTM flg22_FLS2"),
  "Binary FLS2/flg22 modeling" = list(data = data_fls2_flg22, predictor = "Average_ipTM")
)

# Initialize a list to store ROC results
roc_results <- list()
auc_values <- list()

# Calculate ROC curves and AUC for each dataset and predictive metric
for (metric_name in names(metrics)) {
  metric_data <- metrics[[metric_name]]$data
  predictor <- metrics[[metric_name]]$predictor
  
  roc_obj <- roc(response = metric_data$Known_outcome, predictor = metric_data[[predictor]])
  roc_results[[metric_name]] <- roc_obj
  auc_values[[metric_name]] <- auc(roc_obj)
}

# Prepare data for plotting
roc_coords <- lapply(roc_results, function(roc_obj) {
  coords(roc_obj, "all", ret = c("specificity", "sensitivity"))
})

roc_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(roc_coords), function(metric_name) {
  data.frame(
    Metric = metric_name,
    Specificity = 1 - roc_coords[[metric_name]]$specificity,
    Sensitivity = roc_coords[[metric_name]]$sensitivity
  )
}))

# Assign colors for each metric
color_matrix <- c(
  "Full Complex Modeling" = "#845ec2",
  "Binary FLS2/flg22 modeling" = "#5dc4c9"
)

# Custom ggplot theme
my_ggplot_theme <- theme_classic() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20, color = "black"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(size = 0.8),
    legend.position = c(0.66, 0.15),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14)
  )

# Plot the ROC curves using ggplot2
roc_plot <- ggplot(roc_data, aes(x = Specificity, y = Sensitivity, color = Metric)) +
  geom_line(size = 1, show.legend = TRUE) +
  geom_line(data = data.frame(x = c(0, 1), y = c(0, 1)), aes(x, y), linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgrey") +
  scale_color_manual(values = color_matrix, 
                     labels = paste(names(auc_values), "(AUC:", round(unlist(auc_values), 3), ")")) +
  labs(title = "ROC Curves for Predictive Metrics", x = "False Positive Rate", y = "True Positive Rate") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), labels = c("0", "0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "1")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), labels = c("0", "0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "1")) +
  my_ggplot_theme

# Print the plot
print(roc_plot)

# Save the plot
ggsave("../output/af3/ROC_compare_2vs3_complex.pdf", plot = roc_plot, width = 6.5, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```
